## The mistake this prevents

scout-idea-grading (B-04, C-5) made per-lens `wins`/`lost` masses FRACTIONAL —
`winCredit(grade) = (grade − 1) / 4`, so one grade-3 produces `wins: 0.5`.
`upsertScoutLensWeights` ships those rows through
`jsonb_to_recordset(${payload}::text::jsonb) AS x(lens text, wins int, decided int, weight numeric)`.

Everyone (including the in-code docstring) assumed the `int` cast would round.
**It doesn't — PostgreSQL raises** `invalid input syntax for type integer: "0.5"`,
the whole multi-row upsert dies, and because the call sits in a
warn-and-continue `try/catch` ("a weight-upsert failure must not fail the
outcome refresh"), nothing surfaced: every suite passed on the no-error
contract while ANY mid-scale grade in the workspace stranded
`scout_lens_weights` stale in production. Caught only by B-08's composed
integration test (`grading-feedback-loop.integration.test.ts`) via
vitest-fail-on-console tripping on the warn.

## The rules

1. **A best-effort (warn-and-swallow) write is only testable by asserting the
   rows actually landed.** "No error" is precisely the thing the swallow makes
   meaningless. Pin the post-write SELECT (see the `decided=1` regression pin
   in grading-feedback-loop.integration.test.ts, and its older sibling pinning
   the bytes.js Array-serialization failure on the SAME seam — this class
   recurs).
2. **`::int` / recordset `int` columns ERROR on fractional input — they never
   round.** If a JS-side value can be fractional, `Math.round()` it before it
   enters the payload (fixed in `upsertScoutLensWeights`,
   `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/routed-ledger.ts`), or make the column
   `numeric`.

## Symptom signature

- Console (often only visible under fail-on-console): `[scout/routed-ledger]
  lens-weight upsert failed (non-fatal): invalid input syntax for type
  integer: "0.5"`.
- State signature: a `*_weights` / analytics table whose `updated_at` stops
  advancing after a feature that introduced fractional tallies shipped.
